headline: Build confidentiality into intake
image_alt_text: Social asset showing the Hush Line desktop Encryption settings page for a recipient account. The screen includes Proton key import, a Proton email search field, a Search Proton button, and a manual public PGP key entry area, illustrating how confidentiality of disclosures depends on a clear encryption setup.
rationale: The only available fallback candidate is a recipient-shared encryption settings screen. The post uses the required ISO 37002 principle format and frames confidentiality as a repeatable operational step for recipients and staff, while avoiding the recent encryption checklist and onboarding angles.

social.linkedin:
When a source sends a disclosure, the receiving workflow should already be prepared.

Confidentiality is not only a policy word. In Hush Line, recipients and staff can connect their account to an OpenPGP setup from the account area, using Proton lookup or a manual paste. That turns encryption from a one-time launch task into routine upkeep for the intake channel.

Sign up at https://hushline.app, then confirm the account's encryption configuration.
